text:
Maria: Heads up — runtime compatibility question: if we allow hot-swapping model variants across precisions (FP8 <-> INT8 <-> 4bit), do we want a single canonical KV-cache serialization that can be reused across precisions or separate caches with a migration/shim?

Aj: Short answer: reuse is nice for perf but tricky because quantized tensor layouts and scales differ. We should list tradeoffs before picking.

Sandeep: Agree. Reuse saves recomputation on long-context sessions. But we risk correctness if layer-wise reorder/packing changes between quant formats.

Kevin: Proposal A: canonical on-disk header + per-slice payloads with typed blobs. Each blob has a precision tag and a small decoder. At load time runtime either uses blob directly (if precision matches) or runs a fast up/down-cast path for compatible transforms.

Maria: Example header sketch I threw together:```
RDKV
version:2
model_sha256: <hex>
sequence_len: <u32>
num_layers: <u16>
layer_index_table: [offset,u32]*
blob{precision:u8, element_bytes:u8, compressed:u8, checksum:u32}
```
This allows us to store layer blobs independently so we can migrate a subset lazily.

Aj: Love the per-layer blobs. Questions: (1) what is the cost of on-the-fly conversion? (2) can we guarantee bit-exact fallback to FP16 for safety checks?

Sandeep: For (1), conversion cost depends on dimension packing. INT4/INT8->FP16 expand is cheap-ish (mem-bandwidth bound) if we do vectorized kernels. FP8 is trickier because of per-tensor scale + exp bias. We'll need a small quant-decoder kernel. We should quota this in latency SLOs.

Kevin: For (2) we can include a signed checksum and a short digest per-layer to detect mismatch. If checksum fails or model mismatch, we either 1) invalidate the KV for that layer, 2) try best-effort conversion with telemetry flagged, or 3) fall back to full recompute and surface a metric. I favor (2) + metric.

Maria: Operational constraints: we must not blow up memory on Private. So lazy load per-layer on demand is required. Also encryption: KV blobs live in host memory and may be swapped to disk, so include KMS metadata and HMAC.

Aj: Edge case: rolling deploy where newer model uses a different head-layer dim due to patch. Header should include "model_schema_version" and canonical model id. If IDs differ, we invalidate. If schema same but precision differs, we attempt conversion.

Sandeep: Implementation plan suggestion: V1: read-only canonical format + strict validation. V2: add fast runtime conversion pipelines + metrics + opt-in config per-customer to enable hot-swap. V3: background reserialize service to produce native-precision blobs when load frequency high.

Kevin: Tests we need:
- cross-precision roundtrip: produce KV from FP16 path, convert->store as INT8, reload->convert->use, compare logits for 1k prompts (tolerance).
- perf regression: measure latency p50/p95 with conversion enabled for short and long ctx.
- safety: intentional corruption -> ensure invalidation path + no silent bad outputs.

Maria: UX: expose a flag on route config: "kv_compatibility: strict|convert|separate". Default = strict (no silent conversion). Admins can enable convert. Also surface telemetry: converted_layers_count, conversion_ms, invalidated_blobs.

Aj: Runtime API changes: when grabbing KV we add small metadata {model_id, precision, schema_v}. If model_id differs, caller decides to drop KV. We should return a structured reason for drop so console/playback can show cause.

Sandeep: One more: quantization parameters. For FP8 we need per-channel scale+exponent info sometimes. The blob format should support an optional sidecar table for per-channel params. That table must be small and versioned.

Kevin: Security note: if we allow third-party plugins to read/write KV (private deployments), we must validate header strictly — malformed headers could trigger out-of-bounds reads. Add length-prefixed fields and max-limits.

Maria: Ops: add a canary run where converting is enabled only for 5% of traffic and we diff outputs vs strict path. We'll collect degradation_score and token divergence.

Aj: Action items: (1) Sandeep, draft precise header binary layout + example C struct (2) Kevin, prototype convert kernel for INT8<->FP16 and measure perf (3) Ops-bot, create canary plan doc and metrics dashboard.

ops-bot: Created task cards: RDW-2312 (header design), RDW-2313 (convert kernel), RDW-2314 (canary + dashboards).

Sandeep: I'll post a follow-up with struct + decision matrix by EOD tomorrow.

Kevin: Quick note about storage: use chunked blobs aligned to 4k with optional compression (zstd). Compression helps INT4 density but hurts latency; make compress=true opt-in per-route.

Maria: Thanks everyone. This keeps the hot-swap UX simple for customers while letting us iterate on conversion. If there are no objections, I'll put a short RFC PR with header sketch + ops plan.

Aj: No objections from me :thumbsup:

Sandeep: SGTM

Kevin: SGTM :rocket:

Maria: PR incoming.
